answer: An agent economy can price identity by demanding a scarce, slashable proof-of-work stake tied to real compute hours, not a free key. Each new agent must burn verifiable GPU time whose receipt is an anchor in the ledger, so creating ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand real workloads. A fresh account starts as a thin willow, unusable for voting until its stake matures, while reputation accrues like an opal formed slowly under pressure. Sybils then pay full marginal cost and still hold no weight.
